title: Choose the visual world for Analyst Buddy
question: The roll assigned The Monday Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Monday Board
options.lineage: the office whiteboard where every weekly review happens
options.thesis: Every week starts at the board: what the numbers did, why, and who acts.
materials: dry-erase enamel with ghosted old marks
brushed aluminium frame and marker tray
options.viewport: The hero is the board itself in its aluminium frame: this week's numbers in marker, and a magnet-pinned card holding the working request access form.
options.risk: Tips into playful if the marker lettering gets cute; marker type is reserved for numbers and annotations, all copy stays in a sturdy grotesk.

raised.raise: Every figure on the board carries a small source tag: rows read, code run.
One strict grid: the board's ruled lines are the page's layout grid.
Scale with intent: the one number that matters is written five times larger than the rest.
Insights ranked down one lane, most urgent first.
Copy in short blocks, two lines at most, like notes on a board.

options.label: The Markets Page
options.lineage: the business newspaper's markets and companies pages
options.thesis: Your company reported like a market: today's movers, the numbers, the analyst's note.
options.viewport: A front page for one company: banner headline on this week's biggest mover, a movers table, and the request access form set as a subscription coupon.
options.risk: Familiar: broadsheet editorial is where many runs in this category land, and it can read stiff to some owners.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.lineage: the row of needles on a recording desk
options.thesis: Every goal is a needle; you read the business by sweeping the row.
options.viewport: A bridge of goal meters across the top, each needle settling on this week's value; red only past the target line.
options.case: Fuses on clarity: goals as meters read instantly; loses on audience, owners do not live at a mixing desk.
options.risk: Reads as a gadget if the needles move without a real number behind them.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: Follow one number's life from raw row to answer.
options.viewport: One ribbon column tracing a figure through the data.
options.case: Fuses poorly: owners do not identify with museum archives.
options.kept: Every figure carries its source tag.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.viewport: A glyph-rendered chart filling the screen.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reads as code, which scares non-technical owners.

options.label: Tropicalia Sleeve
options.thesis: The business as a pasted-up tableau.
options.viewport: A collage of numbers at mismatched scales.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too playful for numbers owners must trust.

options.label: Moon-shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Insights traded down a moonlit lane.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dreamlike, loses product clarity.

options.label: Village Coffeehouse Identity
options.viewport: A torn-paper header with a stamped mark.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dated, and soft where the voice must be expert.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What AI analytics startups ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and subcopy beside a dashboard screenshot, logo row, feature cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
